recordDecisions.title: SmallRatio: Dedekind sums along Euclid's algorithm and the small-ratio formula
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For a prime p and 0 < h < p, the Dedekind sum s(h,p) is determined, up to an explicit error of order log p, by the fractions of small height congruent to plus or minus h: with the sum over the coprime pairs u, v >= 1 with uv < p/2, |12 s(h,p) - p sum ([hv = u mod p] - [hv = -u mod p])/(uv)| <= 6n <= 12 log_2 p + 6, where n is the length of Euclid's algorithm on (p, h). Summed over any set H of residues, in particular over a subgroup of odd order, this gives |12 sum_{h in H} s(h,p) - p S_H(p)| <= |H| (12 log_2 p + 6), where S_H(p) is the signed sum of 1/(uv) over the coprime pairs with uv < p/2 and u/v in H or -H. The development proves Dedekind reciprocity from scratch (by counting lattice points), the identities of Euclid's algorithm and the bound n <= 2 log_2 k + 1, the alternating-sum form 12 s(h,k) = sum (-1)^{j+1} k/(r_j q_{j-1}) + E with |E| <= 4n, and Legendre's pairing of the small coprime pairs with the steps of the algorithm, by a lattice-basis argument instead of continued fractions.

(18)-(19)); the probability is below 1/2 (the two-qubit, real-settings case of a bound that follows in every dimension from Cereceda 2016, eq. recordDecisions.title: PCF all the way down
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
Let k be a field of characteristic zero and let f: X → X be a finite surjective map of integral k-schemes of finite type. By the critical locus of f we mean the image in X of the critical locus of the map induced on the normalization of X. By the branch locus we mean the image of the critical locus under f.

We say that f is post-critically finite (PCF) if, for every irreducible divisor D contained in the branch locus, the forward orbit f(D) ∪ f^2(D) ∪ … is algebraic, that is, a finite union of subvarieties, taken as a closed subscheme with its reduced induced structure.

We prove that if f is PCF and A is a preperiodic divisor for f with f^{r+s}(A) = f^r(A), then, setting B = f^r(A) and g = f^s, the restriction of g to B is PCF.

This proves the PCF all the way down conjecture: restricting again to preperiodic divisors and iterating gives PCF maps at every stage.

recordDecisions.title: A finite two-temperature lower bound for the GHR sum-difference constant
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The Gyarmati-Hennecart-Ruzsa constant C₃ₐ is the supremum of real exponents theta for which every K > 1 admits a positive constant c and arbitrarily large nonempty finite integer sets X with nonempty partners Y satisfying |X+Y| <= K|X| and c|X+Y|^theta <= |X-Y|. This formalization proves the strict bound C₃ₐ > 60709/50000 = 1.21418. A finite type at depth 10^13, separate difference and sum tilts, cyclic compression, and a proved finite-set principle supply the bound. The result concerns extremal sumset and difference-set growth in additive combinatorics. The paper's general limiting theorem is outside the formalized claim.

recordDecisions.title: Every Run of the Center Column Is Shorter Than Its Start Time
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
For the center column $c$ of rule 30 from a single black cell, a block of black cells that starts at time $a \ge 1$ has length at most $a$ (`Rule30Submission.black_run_le`, tight at $a = 3$), and a block of white cells that starts at time $a \ge 3$ has length at most $a - 3$ (`white_run_le_three`; at most $a - 1$ for every $a \ge 1$, `white_run_le'`, attained only at $a = 2$). Hence every window $[a, 2a)$ holds a black cell and every window $[a, 2a]$ a white one (`exists_black'`, `exists_white`), and $\log_2 n + 1 \le \mathrm{blackCount}\,n$ for $n \ge 1$ (`log_two_succ_le_blackCount`, with the kit's `blackCount` from Problem 2). recordDecisions.title: Exact XOR Superposition Rigidity for Rule 30
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
For every two ordinary Rule 30 histories $A,B:\mathbb N\times\mathbb Z\to\{0,1\}$, their pointwise XOR is itself a Rule 30 history if and only if $A=0$, $B=0$, or $A=B$. The equalities concern complete histories, with no finite support, boundary or periodicity hypotheses. `Rule30Submission.xor_history_iff` states the recurrence explicitly; `Rule30Submission.standard_two_partners` gives exactly the two partners of every nonzero history.

The proposed kit contribution is this general superposition classification. The comparison kit, commit `2f63afda261888e04ec57237290e723190914a1d`, supplies ordinary Rule 30 evolution in `Rule30Jen` and the prize statements in `Rule30Prize`. The one-step quadratic mixed-product identity is background algebra, also noted in [Dibujaron's public Rule 30 notes](https://github.com/Dibujaron/rule30); maps commuting with Rule 30 were constrained by Coven, Hedlund and Rhodes (1979), whose map-level results do not classify individual history pairs. Historical priority for the classification is not asserted.

Encode a synchronized pair of Boolean states as a four-color vector. The local cross defect is the determinant of adjacent vectors. Strong induction on the separation between incompatible nonzero colors shows that an intervening zero gap cannot persist. Restricting at arbitrary integer roots removes the half-line boundary freedom, and a linear coordinate shear returns to ordinary Rule 30.

This is a structural partial result related to the prize, not a proof of center-column nonperiodicity, balance, or computational complexity. No quantitative collision-time bound or affine four-history classification is claimed.

recordDecisions.title: A Half-Rate Exponent Bound for Right-Diagonal Periods in Rule 30
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
For Rule 30 grown from one black cell, let $R(j,t)=\mathrm{cell}(t,t-j)$. For every $j,t\ge0$, we prove $R(j,t+2^{B(j)})=R(j,t)$ (`Rule30Submission.right_period`), where $B(j)=\lceil j/2\rceil+Q_0(\lfloor j/2\rfloor)$. This uniform result improves the exponent coefficient $2/3$ in the pinned kit's `Rule30RightPeriods.per_upper`. It also improves Nersissian's Fibonacci ceiling, whose coefficient is approximately $0.69424$.

The mechanism tracks the multiplicity at $1$ of a temporal polynomial over $\mathbf F_2$ along the black-wall map $\mathrm{PhiS}\,3$. Exposing two more bits multiplies a cycle length by $1$, $2$, or $4$. Multiplication by $4$ resets a resource exponentially, while multiplication by $2$ reduces it by at most one. An inductive record invariant yields the inverse-tower correction.

Optimality and worldwide priority are not certified. None of Prize Problems 1–3 is resolved.

recordDecisions.title: A finite-depth right edge follows the single-cell ruler with a fixed cap
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
For every finite nonzero row $x$ of rule 30, read from its rightmost black cell $e$ (bit $k$ of the edge code is $x(e-k)$), the edge advances one cell per step and the code evolves by the 2-adic edge map $T$ of Coven, Pivato and Yassawi (`edge_evol`). For rows of finite orbit depth, we prove the following capped-ruler theorem. Suppose the code agrees with the single cell's code at time $s_0$ on bits $0,\dots,k-1$, for some $k \ge 2$, while no code of the single cell's orbit agrees with it on bits $0,\dots,k$. Then at every time $t$ the code agrees with the single cell's code at time $s_0+t$ below bit $k$ and differs at bit $k$. Its white run behind the edge cell equals the single cell's when that run is shorter than $k-1$, is exactly $k-1$ when the single cell's is at least $k-1$, and is never longer (`frozen_ruler`). The single cell's code never has a white run of exactly $k-1$ (`no_width_at_depth`), so the cut width lies in a gap of the ruler. Every row has a depth, or agrees with the orbit at every depth (`depth_dichotomy`).

The kit's `Rule30RightPeriods` describes the single cell's right diagonals; this gives a conditional capped-ruler theorem and a depth dichotomy for arbitrary right-edge codes. The proof uses only the triangularity of $T$, with no counting of periods.

Not claimed: anything about the center column or the Prize problems, or that rows of infinite depth are the single cell's own rows (open).

recordDecisions.title: Staircases near the single cell's right edge end; the rain rows keep a two-step edge patch for ever
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
In rule 30 grown from one black cell, call a maximal alternating stretch of length at least $3$ a staircase. Its interior keeps its colors, and its front is eaten one cell per row (`front_step`), so a living staircase keeps its distance $W$ from the advancing right edge. recordDecisions.title: White runs beside two periodic columns of rule 30 are at most two periods long

recordDecisions.title: The left diagonals of rule 30: their periods are unbounded, and the settled band has no long white run
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
The catalog proves that every left diagonal $D_j(t) = c(t,\, j - t)$ of the rule 30 pattern is eventually periodic, with a period dividing $2^j$ (`Rule30Diagonals.D_periodic`). This essay proves what the periods can be. For every configuration with a leftmost black cell:

- **Lemma B1.** No two adjacent left diagonals are both eventually white, and an eventually white diagonal is followed, two later, by an eventually black one (`seed_no_adjacent_white`, `seed_white_then_black`).
- **Lemma B2.** No $P \ge 1$ is an eventual period of every left diagonal: among the first $4^P + 2$ diagonals, one does not have eventual period $P$. So the eventual periods are unbounded, and infinitely many diagonals are eventually white and infinitely many eventually black (`seed_periods_unbounded`, `seed_periods_unbounded_quant`, `seed_infinitely_many_white`, `seed_infinitely_many_black`).
- **Lemma B3.** If the diagonals $0, \dots, M$ have had a common period $P$ for $P$ steps, then a white run of the row inside them that is bounded on the left by a black diagonal has length at most $2P - 1$ (`lemma_B3_sharp`).

recordDecisions.title: A repeat on the center column cannot put its white run inside the settled band of left diagonals
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
Jen's theorem with a clock, the catalog's `window_jen_col`, bounds a block of length $n$ that columns $0$ and $1$ share at times $a < a_2$ by $n \le a_2$. The bound comes from a white run: row $a_2$ is white at the distances $a + 1, \dots, n - 1$ left of the center, which lie on the left diagonals $a_2 - n + 1, \dots, a_2 - a - 1$. This essay proves that the run cannot lie in the band of diagonals that has settled.

**Theorem $\mathrm{A}''''$.** If the diagonals $0, \dots, M$ agree at times $a_2 - P$ and $a_2$, with $1 \le P \le a_2$ and $M < a_2 - a$, then $n \le L + a_2 - M + 2P - 1$, for every configuration with a leftmost black cell $L$ cells left of the column (`theorem_A4_sharp`; for the single seed, with the kit's `cell` and `Rule30Diagonals.D`, `center_A4_sharp`).

The tool is Lemma B3 (`lemma_B3_sharp`): inside such a band, a white run bounded on the left by a black diagonal has length at most $2P - 1$, and the run of Theorem $\mathrm{A}'''$ has a black diagonal on its left, since diagonal $0$, the edge, is black. The kit has the clocked bound and the bound $2^j$ on the period of each left diagonal, but nothing that joins them. Nothing here decides Problem 1.

recordDecisions.title: Under a period-2 center column, a right neighbour that starts with near-squares has no left edge
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
The first open case of Problem 1 is period 2: the center column reads the clock $0101\ldots$ from some time on. Under that clock, the left-permutivity of rule 30 determines column $-1$ from column $1$: black at odd times, and the complement of column $1$ at even times. A configuration with a leftmost black cell whose column $0$ reads the clock from some time $T_0$ has no near-squares at unbounded scales in its visible bits: there is no constant $K$ with pairs $i < i_2$, $i_2 - i$ unbounded, whose common future lasts $i_2 - K$ steps.

The visible agreement gives columns $-1$ and $0$ a common block of length $2(i_2 - K)$, and an eventually black diagonal $b \ge L + 2K$ bounds it by $2i_2 - 2K - 1$.

recordDecisions.title: Rule 210 beside the period-2 clock: the one-sided question is false and the left half is linear
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
The catalog's `Rule30ZeroBoundary.Q01` is the period-2 question for rule 30 in one-sided form: no finitely supported start of the zero-boundary left half keeps column $-1$ black at every even step. The reason is a parity invariant (`parity_invariant`): for every start consistent with the clock, every black cell at time $t$ and depth $k$ has $t + k$ even. So no two horizontally adjacent cells are both black, the gate $\lnot c \land r$ reduces to $r$, and the left half evolves as rule 90 does, linearly (`linear`).

recordDecisions.title: Every Sturmian word, of every slope and every intercept, is excluded as the right neighbour of a period-2 center column
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
For every irrational slope $0 \le \alpha < 1$ and every intercept $\theta$, the mechanical word $m_{\alpha,\theta}(i) = \lfloor \theta + (i+1)\alpha \rfloor - \lfloor \theta + i\alpha \rfloor$ is not the sequence of visible bits of any configuration with a leftmost black cell $L \ge 1$ cells left of the center whose center column reads the clock $0101\ldots$ from some time $T_0$ on: $\mathrm{evol}\,x_0\,(2i)\,1 = m_{\alpha,\theta}(i)$ for all $i$ is impossible (`Rule30Submission.sturmian_excluded`; the clock from time $0$ without the condition on $L$, `sturmian_excluded_clock0`; the fractional-part form $m(i) = [1 - \alpha \le \{\theta + i\alpha\}]$, `sturmian_excluded_fract`). The same holds for every block code of the word (`sturmian_block_excluded`).

The catalog reduces period 2 to `Rule30ZeroBoundary.Q01` and says nothing about the right neighbour of a clocked center column. Our submission R30-20261023-0c4a33 excluded the characteristic words, intercept $0$, through the standard words; this essay removes that restriction with a combinatorial argument.

A Sturmian word has at most $n + 1$ distinct blocks of length $n$, so two of the $n + 2$ blocks starting at positions $0, \ldots, n + 1$ coincide (`exists_block_collision`, by the pigeonhole principle on threshold sets); irrationality keeps the two positions far apart as $n$ grows (`no_small_period`), which gives near-squares with slack $1$ at unbounded scales (`sturmian_pairs`). Shifting the intercept by $T_0 \alpha$ moves the clock's start to time $0$, and Corollary F (R30-20261022-91b0b0) forbids such near-squares.

Nothing is claimed for rational slopes, nor for any right neighbour that is not a block code of a Sturmian word.

recordDecisions.title: The channel bound at width 14: explicit automaton states, one kernel check per state
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
For every configuration $x : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ whose center column reads the clock, $\mathrm{evol}\,x\,t\,0 = [t \text{ odd}]$ for all $t$, the first $n$ visible bits $\mathrm{visFrom}\,x\,0\,n$ (column $1$ at the even times) lie in one set $S$ of words with $|S| \cdot 10^{9n} \le 300 \cdot 1184655442^{\,n}$ (`Rule30Submission.channel_bound_14`): about $0.2445$ bits of information per visible bit asymptotically ($\log_2(1184655442/10^9) \approx 0.24447$, with a finite correction $\log_2 300 / n$).

The catalog reduces period 2 to `Rule30ZeroBoundary.Q01` and has nothing about the right neighbour of a clocked column. Our submission R30-20261023-4767e0 proved this bound at width $12$ ($0.258$ bits) by rebuilding the window automaton inside one kernel computation; that does not scale, since the kernel's caches live for one declaration. Here the certificate is explicit: the bitset of each of the $919$ states of the width-$14$ automaton, its graph and Collatz-Wielandt weights.

One theorem per state (`s14_i`) has the kernel sweep the state's bitset and check that every member's four two-step images, with the cell beyond the window at the two successive times as free inputs, lie in the successor of its label (`stateCheck`); `explicit_sound` assembles the $919$ theorems into the closure of every edge, `bound_of` and `weight_bound` give the bound, and `win_step2` ties the window to the kit's `evol`. The sets are checked data, not derived: any family with the root full and every edge closed bounds the words.

Nothing here decides `Q01`: the bound measures the right neighbour. Width $16$ (about $0.2131$ bits) would need about $45$ MB of state literals in this form and is not attempted.

recordDecisions.title: Sparse16: A Finite Obstruction to an Alternating Center in Rule 30

recordDecisions.title: Left-Cone Reconstruction Lemmas and Complete Classification of Jen's Left-Permutive Class in Rule30Realization
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
For the general left-permutive cellular automaton family `run (g : Bool -> Bool -> Bool)` in `Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Realization`, Jen's adjacent-column theorem `run_not_adjacent` assumes `g false false = false` and `g false true = true`. We prove that a Boolean function `g` satisfies these two hypotheses if and only if `g = g90 \lor g = g150 \lor g = g210 \lor g = g30` (`Rule30Submission.jen_class_iff_four_rules`). Within this four-element class, we prove three exact equivalences for the single-seed evolution `run g`: (1) `\forall t\,p,\, run g t p = run g90 t p` holds if and only if `g = g90 \lor g = g210` (`Rule30Submission.run_eq_run90_iff_g90_or_g210`); (2) the single-seed pattern is mirror-symmetric (`\forall t\,p,\, run g t (-p) = run g t p`) if and only if `g = g90 \lor g = g150 \lor g = g210` (`Rule30Submission.run_symm_iff_not_g30`); and (3) the center column `fun t => run g t 0` is not eventually constant (`\lnot \exists T\,b,\, \forall t \ge T,\, run g t 0 = b`) if and only if `g = g30` (`Rule30Submission.g30_unique_nonconstant_in_jen_class`).

In addition, we prove explicit multi-step left-cone reconstruction lemmas extending `Rule30Jen.cell_left` and `Rule30Realization.lc`: a closed-form two-step formula for `cell t (p - 2)` (`Rule30Submission.tlf_cell_two_step_left_retrodiction`), all-depth left-cone uniqueness by strong induction on `k : \mathbb{N}` for any two trajectories obeying `rule` that agree on two adjacent columns (`Rule30Submission.tlf_left_cone_unique_all_depths`), and exact agreement of the recursive left-reconstruction operator `lc seed center m t` with `cell t (-m)` (`Rule30Submission.lc_seed_eq_cell`, `Rule30Submission.lc_seed_triangle_and_diag`).

recordDecisions.title: A three-fifths bound on black runs in the rule 30 center column
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: We prove in Lean that a black run of the rule 30 center column lasts at most about three fifths of its starting time: if c(a) = … = c(a + L − 1) = 1 with a ≥ 1, then L ≤ a − 2⌊(a − 1)/5⌋, hence 5L ≤ 3a + 10 (headline `Rule30Submission.black_run_three_fifths`). The kit's catalog had L ≤ a (`Rule30CenterRuns.black_run_le`). As consequences, every window [a, (8a + 10)/5] contains a white cell, so there are about log_{8/5} n white cells before time n, where the catalog had ⌊log₄ n⌋; the argument also bounds alternating blocks anywhere in the light cone and, relative to the first black cell right of the center, white runs. Under a black run the row at time a alternates. Going back in time, left-permutivity rebuilds each earlier row from the later one and two unknown cells; whatever those cells are, the alternation heals four cells further out, so after s steps the row alternates on cells 4s to L − 1 + s left of the center. After ⌊(a − 1)/5⌋ steps this block would contain the two adjacent black cells of the left edge, which is impossible. The four-cell healing is in `Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripe.agrees_pre`; what is new is its use on a finite block together with the left edge. We claim no unconditional bound of slope below 1 for white runs, and nothing sublinear: 3/5 is the limit of this method.

recordDecisions.title: Period-32 two-phase shielding rigidity for finite Rule 30 moving-front states
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
Let $D(x)_k = x_k \oplus (x_{k+1} \lor x_{k+2})$ be the triangular map of `Rule30ControlledResponse`: the right half of rule 30 seen in a frame moving one cell per step. For every state $x : \mathbb{N} \to \{0,1\}$ that is zero from some cell $W$ on, if $D^{32}x = x$ and the alternating shielding gates hold (for every $t < 32$, $(D^t x)_0 \lor (D^t x)_1$ when $t$ is even and $(D^t x)_0$ when $t$ is odd), then $D^2 x = x$ (`Rule30Submission.period_thirtytwo_reduces_to_two`). For an integer $n$ with $T(n) = n \oplus ((n \gg 1) \lor (n \gg 2))$, $T^{32}(n) = n$ and the same gates on its bits, $n$ is a canonical stripe $U_w$ for some $w$ (`Rule30Submission.period_thirtytwo_gate_stripe`). No bound on the width $W$ is assumed.

The catalog's `Rule30FiniteClockCertificate` proves generic soundness of finite temporal-profile pools, and `Rule30FiniteClockSixteen` applies it to full clocks dividing 16. This applies it at clock 32 under the gates and adds the stripe classification.

Method: a pool of 2,116 temporal pairs of 32-periodic columns, closed under left extension and checked by the kernel in 67 blocks, covers every finite width. On gated pairs the head has period 2, and a detection check carries that clock to the whole state. A 14-state certificate over an eight-state stripe automaton then identifies the period-2 integer profiles as stripes.

Not claimed: the result is conditional on the 32-step return and on the gates. It excludes no period of the center column and solves no Rule 30 Prize problem.

recordDecisions.title: Least Period 4 of Rule 30: a Weaker Sufficient Condition, and Why the Left Half Must Be Finite
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Problem 1 asks whether the center column of rule 30 is ever eventually periodic. The kit reduces the three words of least period 4 (0001, 0011, 0111) to the open statement Absorption (Rule30Ether): every finite right half driven by the word must eventually enter a family of ether-and-wall states. The kit's proof only uses a consequence of that entry, which we isolate as Lock w: every finite right half driven by w^∞ has column 1 eventually periodic at the white times of the driver (with any period 4Q), or some column q ≥ 1 eventually periodic. We prove in Lean that Lock w excludes w^∞ as a tail of the center column whatever the transient (Rule30Submission.lock_excludes, by masked Jen or by Jen), that the kit's Absorption implies Lock (lock_of_absorption), and that the three locks exclude least period 4 (least_period_four_of_lock). Lock is open for the three words, but it no longer mentions the ether, the wall or any entry state. Second, the proof uses the finiteness of the left half (through Jen), and that hypothesis cannot be weakened to spatial periodicity, even with a finite right half: for each of the three words, and for the alternating column 1, 0, 1, 0, …, there is a configuration whose left half is the 7-periodic ether and whose right half is finite (ether columns, one of the kit's wall states, then white), with center column exactly the word from time 0 (period_four_left_periodic_right_finite, alt_left_periodic_right_finite). recordDecisions.title: Rule 30: Self-Shielded Black Runs, Sharper White-Run Bounds, and Q01 as an Integer Iteration
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Problem 1 asks whether the center column of rule 30 is ever eventually periodic. We prove three partial results in Lean, against the current kit. **Self-shielding.** By the kit's Lemma A* (`Rule30BlackRuns.black_shield`), a black run of length 9j in the center column forces the pattern (white, black)^j in columns 1..2j. This pattern shields itself: it moves two columns to the right every two steps without reading the cell on its right, so for 2j steps after the run the columns 1..2j depend only on the center column, and column 1 is determined for 4j steps instead of the 2j of the light cone. With masked Jen this halves the slope of the kit's Theorems B and D: if the center column is eventually P-periodic, it has no black run of length r < P followed by a white cell with 9⌈(P−r)/4⌉ ≤ r (`Rule30Submission.no_long_black_run_quarter`; the kit needs 9⌈(P−r+9)/2⌉ ≤ r), and similarly for a black run followed by a white run (`no_black_white_run_quarter`). So every word 1^r u with 1 ≤ |u| ≤ 4 and u starting white is excluded for r ≥ 9 (`no_black_run_ge9_len_le4`; the kit's `Rule30BlackRunBlocks` needs r ≥ 18 or 27 for its eight blocks), and every 1^r u with |u| ≤ 8 for r ≥ 18. **White runs.** Theorem W′ (`no_white_run_block`) excludes 0^r (1 :: v) as the eventual period from two finite kernel-checked certificates. It gives eight tails with sharper bounds than the catalog: r ≥ 12 for 1011, 10011, 11011, 101011 and 110011, r ≥ 20 for 111001, r ≥ 21 for 100011 and 111011 (the catalog: 49, 61 or 71). **An integer form of Q01.** One step of the kit's zero-boundary left half, read as a binary number, is F(Y) = ⌊Y/2⌋ XOR (Y OR 2Y), and the kit's open condition Q01, which excludes period 2, holds iff every natural number Y reaches an even number under some iterate of G = F∘F (`Q01_iff_integer`). F is tied to the kit's moving-frame map Φ(Y) = Y XOR (2Y OR 4Y) by Φ(Y) = 2F(Y) + (Y mod 2). Numerically every Y < 2^16 reaches an even number within 16 steps of G. None of this excludes period 2, 3 or 4: their words have no black run of length 9, and Q01 stays open.

recordDecisions.title: Left-Diagonal Defect Spectra, Sublinear Monochromatic Run Bounds, and Semigroup Saturation in Rule 30
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
This submission presents Emerson Villafuerte's verified work on diagonal defect spectra and run bounds across 88 kernel-verified theorems.

Key results and clarifications:
1. Universal Black Run Bound: for all a >= 4, every black run on the center column satisfies L <= a - 2 (`black_run_center_le_ge4`), strictly improving Morales's linear bound L <= a. As noted in peer review, this bound is strictly stronger than the three-fifths bound of R30-20261025-0554f7 (L <= a - 2 Floor[(a - 1)/5]) at a = 4 (2 < 4) and a = 5 (3 < 5).
2. Recurrence Window: every interval [a, 2a - 2] holds a white cell (`exists_white_ge4`), contracting Morales's [a, 2a].
3. Conditional White Row Bound: diagonal defect theorems establish conditional bounds on alternating triangular preRow row blocks (`white_run_le_diag5`: L <= a - 5 whenever ell + 7 <= a). Per reviewer guidance, this is not an unconditional bound on center-column white runs, for which no bound L <= a - 5 holds since c(6) = c(7) = 0.
4. Diagonal Defect Spectrum: exact closed-form period determinations D_2(t+2) = false, D_3(t+2) = [t = 1 mod 2], D_4(t+2) = true, and D_5(t+3) = [t = 0 mod 2], with defect theorems bounding runs by a - j.
5. Preserved Foundation: Semigroup saturation excluding 22 infinite repeating-word families (8 white-run 0^q u, 14 black-run 1^r u), universal period-2 dichotomy, unconditional solutions of CQEmpty across all phases for period-4 words (0001, 0011, 0111) and period-3 (001), bounded-width Q001 (W <= 12), and depth-1000 sideways certifications.

recordDecisions.title: Partial structural results toward Rule 30 Problem 1: a truncation bridge, first kernel-checked Q001 instances, and a coupled golden-mean source constraint
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
**Result.** Partial results toward Problem 1, via the kit's left-half reductions `Q01` (period 2) and `Q001` (least period 3). A generic truncation bridge, `constrained_black_window`: a width-$d$ death bound $D$ forces a black cell at a depth in $(d, D+1]$ in *every* row whose column $-1$ matches a fixed pattern on a time-set forever  finite or infinite rows alike. Instances: `black_window_52` (a black cell in $(d, 97]$ for every $d \le 52$) and the period-3 `q001_black_window`. The first kernel-checked instances of `Q001`: `q001_cases_up_to_16`, `q001_width_le_16`. An equivalence upgrade, `q001_iff_finite_dies`: `Q001` holds iff every finitely supported zero-boundary start has column $-1$ white at some step $3j$. **New relative to the catalog.** The kit has no kernel-checked `Q001` instances (its evidence is a non-kernel C search); the truncation-bridge and black-window statements, and the coupled adjacent-black-source ($11$-free) structure, are absent from the catalog.

Triangular truncation turns any width-$d$ kernel death bound into an unconditional black-window statement for infinite constrained rows; the `Q001` instances are kernel-checked finite case analyses; `adjSrc_factor_le_fib` uses the elementary count of $11$-free words, $\mathrm{fib}(n+2)$.

recordDecisions.title: Periodic temporal profiles of rule 30: pulse holes, source weights and rooted returns
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: We study Boolean temporal profiles related by the rule 30 left-diagonal recurrence C(t+1) = A(t) XOR (B(t) OR C(t)). `Rule30Submission.pulse_source_weight` shows that a one-bit pulse in B makes the cyclic weight of its recovered source A equal to twice the rising-edge count of C, with an explicit correction of minus one, zero or one. `Rule30Submission.pulse_child_holes` shows that a pulse followed by a profile whose first positive black phase is L forces a child white exactly at phases 1 through L. For q-periodic profiles with q at least 4, `Rule30Submission.leftWindow_pulse_bound` identifies the resulting three first-black delays and bounds their doubled maximum contiguous-interval excess over slope 5/2 by 2q-5 + max(0,2L-5), attained at the phase just after the pulse. Separately, `Rule30Submission.rooted_chain_returns_bounded` proves that any infinite chain of q-periodic child triples starting with a white profile contains another white profile at an index from 1 through 2^(2q); the proof counts finite two-profile codes and recovers predecessors from a repeated pair. Reset existence and uniqueness (`Rule30Submission.child_exists`, `Rule30Submission.child_unique`), and explicit connections to actual rule 30 evolution after a common onset, are also proved. These are conditional profile statements. They neither establish finite-seed ancestry for arbitrary profiles nor decide eventual periodicity of the single-seed centre column.

recordDecisions.title: Finite-arc rotation codes beside a Rule 30 clock
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Suppose a Rule 30 row has its leftmost black cell at -L, with L a natural number, and column 0 is white at even times and black at odd times from time 0. We prove its visible neighbour x(1,2s) cannot eventually equal a binary finite-step coding of an irrational circle rotation when continued-fraction digits exceed 2^(r+1) arbitrarily late, with r supplied endpoint labels. A window-Jen bound forces frequent mismatches; finite pigeonhole and continuant determinant spacing contradict that bound. Arbitrary endpoint values are allowed because an irrational orbit visits each listed endpoint at most once. A concrete union of k half-open intervals has threshold 2^(2k+1), counting its 2k supplied labels. The proof formalizes the record's general-arc extension; earlier Sturmian/block-code exclusions cover special cases. No all-irrational rotation, eventual physical-clock restart or prize result is claimed.

recordDecisions.title: An All-Time Forbidden Return-Gap Pattern in the Alternating-Driven Rule 30 Right Orbit
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:
We prove an all-time restriction on a driven subsystem that arises in the period-two case of Problem 1. Let `u R1` be the kit's sideways observation (`Rule30PeriodTwoSideways.u`) of the right half whose center boundary is driven by the alternating sequence $1,0,1,0,\ldots$, started from the right seed black only at position 1. Record the first-return gaps between consecutive black observations. Every gap is 3 or 5, the first three gaps are 5, and the gap sequence contains the factor $3,5,3,5,3,5,3$ at no index (`Rule30Submission.alternating_R1_no_3535353`). The factors $3,3$ and $3,5,5,3$ are excluded at every index as well.

Relative to the kit catalog and earlier submissions, which give eventual 3/5 spacing for the empty right seed and finite-window obstructions for an alternating center, the new content is the all-index exclusion of this seven-gap word for the one-cell right seed. The exclusions of $3,3$ and $3,5,5,3$ come from our earlier work and are not claimed as new.

Method: the odd-time driven right half is projected to an 18-cell window whose two unseen outer inputs are left free, giving a finite nondeterministic relaxation. A 2,040-state inductive invariant pool, 3,010 first-return edges, a 30-subset deterministic reader and a nine-state monitor show that no relaxed history realizes a forbidden factor; the kit's packed-prefix theorems transfer this to the actual orbit.

Not claimed: nonperiodicity of the free center column, $\neg\,\mathrm{FinSupp}(\Psi\,R_1)$, exclusion of eventual period two, or a solution of any Prize problem.

One further backward step (`bstep1 K` or `bstep0 K`) maps any `(100)^infty` wave to its bitwise complement `(011)^infty` (period 3), and the next step (`bstep0 K`) doubles the spatial period from 3 to 6, locking into `(000101)^infty` (`wave_011_to_period6_step0`).
